reason: It reads like a lot of what I want, but one developer at version 0.4 with no plug-in system makes me unwilling to move my whole setup onto it. I'd install the portable zip and see how it handles my RAW folders, but IrfanView stays the default.
why_switch_or_not: The things that interest me are RAW and JPG showing as separate pictures, the gallery with batch rename/convert, and the editor with white balance, curves and sidecar edits, because I'd like one app for culling and light fixes. But I'd be giving up my IrfanView plug-ins and shortcuts, and I reinstall Windows every year or two. I won't build my workflow around something that may be abandoned, so I'd have to trust it a lot more before it becomes my default.
current_app_pros: IrfanView is tiny and fast enough. I know all the shortcuts. My plug-ins are already set up. Batch convert and rename work the way I expect. It has been stable for years and I never have to think about it.
current_app_pains: Rapid next/back through big RAW folders is slow when I'm culling. The interface looks dated. RAW handling relies on plug-ins and is not great. The editing tools are basic, so I still bounce to another app for real corrections.
objection: One developer, version 0.4. Will it still be maintained next year, and will my edits and sidecar files still open if it is dropped?
would_change_my_mind: A year or more of regular updates, a public roadmap, and a documented, open sidecar format so my edits are not locked in. Seeing it hold up on a few hundred of my RAW+JPG shoots would help too.
